context:
Goal: one definition of "the machine is loaded" for the guard and the sim gatekeeper (your item 304 a).
Problem (rule): your two rulings disagree. The load brake must never read the load average: the Mac read 107 on 15 cores while half idle. Your sim rules of Nov 2 are load-average bars: the 5-minute load under 100 to boot, and slot 2 under 60.
Based on (ruling): decision machine-load-brake.
Based on (ruling): sim-lease-tool item 3 (owner, 2026-11-02 14:28 CST).
Departs from: sim-lease, which grants on load average — grants on memory and disk (a), or the guard also reads the load average (b).
Meanwhile: the lane builds a.
holds: What the shared machine-load definition reads.

options.how: The shared definition reads memory and disk. The sim gatekeeper drops its load-average bars.
options.label: Memory and disk only
options.lose: A Mac with a high CPU load but free memory can boot a simulator.

options.gain: The sim bars stay as you set them on Nov 2.
options.how: The shared definition also reads the load average, so the sim bars stay.
options.label: Add the load average
options.lose: The guard refuses lanes on an idle Mac at load 107.

reply: You picked a: the shared load definition reads memory and disk only. Sent to lane one-load-definition at 15:47 CST Nov 6; home: decision machine-load-brake. Closed 12:12 CST Nov 7.
title: One shared load definition (your item 304 a): drop the load average, or add it to the guard?
why: Your two rulings disagree, so one shared definition must drop one side.
